source_text: Ὅσον οὖν ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη οὐκ ἔρχεται οὐκ ἦσαν παλαιοὶ οἱ προφῆται, οὐδαμοῦ γὰρ παρὰ διαθήκην, εἴρηται πρὸ τούτου· Χριστὸς δέ ἐστιν ὁ παλαιῶν ὄρη, Μωσέα καὶ τοὺς προφήτας. Καὶ οὐκ οἴδασι· Τίνες οὖν οὐκ οἴδασιν; ἐκεῖνοι πρὸς οὓς ἔλεγεν· Εἰ ἐπιστεύετε Μωσεῖ, ἐπιστεύετε ἐν ἐμοί· περὶ ἐμοῦ γὰρ ἐκεῖνος ἐγράφη. Εἰ εἴδησαν Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι περιπαλαιῶται τὰ ὄρη, καταλιπόντες ἂν αὐτὰ, τουτέστιν τὴν τοῦ γράμματος παλαιότητα, διήλλανται καὶ ἐληλύθησαν ἐπὶ τὴν καινὴν διαθήκην· καὶ ἐλάτρευον Θεῷ ἐν καινότητι Πνεύματος, καὶ οὐ παλαιότητι γράμματος· ἐπάγει οὖν· οὐκ οἴδασιν οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι οὔτε τὸν παλαιώσαντα, οὔτε τὰ πεπαλαιωμένα. Διὸ ὁ καταστρέφων, φησὶν, αὐτὰ ὀργῇ, τουτέστι τὴν κατὰ τὸ γράμμα Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἢ τοῦ γράμματος. Ποῦ τὸ αἰσθητὸν θυσιαστήριον; Παράδοξον ὁ Ἰησοῦς μου πεποίηκεν; ἐλθὼν τοὺς αὐτοῦ προφήτας καὶ πεπαλαίωκεν καὶ ἀνεκαίνισε, πεπαλαίωκε, πῶς; ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ ἐν γράμματι ἐντετυπωμένη ἦν, φησίν· ἀνεκαίνισε, πῶς; ὁ μὲν νόμος, φησὶν, ἅγιος καὶ ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ ἁγία καὶ δικαία καὶ ἀγαθή· ἀλλ' οὐκ ἤδεισαν ταῦτα οἱ μὴ μαθόντες τὸ ὄνομα πνευματικόν. 24 Ὁ σείων τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανὸν ἐκ θεμελίων. Χριστός ἐστιν ὁ σείσας τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανόν· πολλοὶ ἐκ μέρους γίνονται σεισμοί· σεῖσμος γέγονεν ἐνθάδε· ἀλλ' οἱ ἐν τῇ πλησίον πόλει οὐκ ἔγνωσαν· ἐπὶ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ οὐ γέγονε μερικῶς, διὰ τοῦτο ὁ σείων τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανὸν ἐκ θεμελίων· οἱ δὲ στύλοι αὐτῆς σαλεύοντες, δηλονότι οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τοῦ πάθους ἐσαλεύθησαν Πάντες ὑμεῖς, φησὶ, σκανδαλισθήσεσθε ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ταύτῃ. ῃ. 7. Ὁ λέγων τῷ ἡλίῳ, καὶ οὐκ ἀνατέλλει, κατὰ δὲ ἄστρων κατασφραγίζει. Καὶ τοῦτο ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ γέγονε· Κατὰ δὲ ἄστρων κατασφραγίζει· φέρεται ὅτι ταῖς τρισὶν ὥραις ἐν αἷς ἐξέλιπεν ὁ ἥλιος, ἀστέρες ἐφάνησαν ἐν οὐρανῷ ὡς ἐν νυκτί. Ὁ ποιῶν Πλειάδα, καὶ Ἕσπερον, καὶ Ἀρκτοῦρον, καὶ Ταμεῖα Νότου. Ταῦτα ὑπὲρ ἐμέ ἐστι τὰ μαθήματα. Πολλῶν γὰρ ὄντων τῶν ἀστέρων Πλειάδων, πλανητῶν καὶ ἀπλάνων παραλεγομένων ὑπὸ τῶν μὴ εἰδότων ὡς αὐτοὶ νομίζουσιν (ἔστι καὶ Ἕσπερος, ἐστι καὶ Φαέτων, καὶ Φαίνων, καὶ Στίλβων καὶ Φωσφόρος) τί δήποτε οὖν ὁ Ἰὼβ ἐν Πνεύματι φθεγγόμενος ἀπὸ τοσούτων ἀστέρων τῶν ἐν τῷ ἀπλάνει τὴν Πλείαδα μόνην ὠνόμασε; καὶ ἀπὸ τοσούτων πλανητῶν λεγομένων Ἕσπερον μόνον εἴρηκε; καὶ ἄλλον ἕνα τὸν Ἀρκτοῦρον τὸν ἐν τῷ ἀρκτοῦν ὄντα, τὸν λεγόμενον ὑπό τινων ἀρκτοφύλακα;
thought_title: Christ ages and renews the prophets; the cosmic signs of the passion
orientation: Athanasius continues interpreting Job's cosmic language, explaining that Christ is the one who ages the mountains (the prophets) and shakes the whole world, with the apostles as its pillars, and that the darkening of the sun and appearance of stars at the crucifixion fulfill Job's words.
pass_a_gloss: So as long as the new covenant does not come, the prophets were not old, for nowhere is it said before this, except in reference to a covenant: but Christ is the one making old the mountains, Moses and the prophets. And they do not know. Who then do not know? Those to whom he was saying: If you believed Moses, you would believe in me; for that one wrote about me. If the Jews had known that the mountains are being made old, having left them, that is the oldness of the letter, they would have been changed and would have come to the new covenant; and they would have worshipped God in newness of Spirit, and not in oldness of letter; he adds then: the Jews do not know then either the one who made old, or the things that have been made old. Therefore the one who overturns, he says, them in wrath, that is the Jerusalem according to the letter or of the letter. Where is the perceptible altar? Has my Jesus done a paradoxical thing? Having come he both made his prophets old and renewed them; he made them old, how? The ministry of death was engraved in letters, it says; he renewed them, how? The law, it says, is holy and his commandment holy and just and good; but those who did not learn the spiritual name did not know these things. 24 The one who shakes what is under heaven from its foundations. Christ is the one who shook what is under heaven; many earthquakes happen in part; an earthquake happened here; but those in the nearby city did not know; but in the case of Christ it did not happen partially, therefore the one who shakes what is under heaven from its foundations; and its pillars are shaken, clearly the apostles were shaken at the time of the passion. All of you, he says, will be scandalized in me this night. 7. The one who says to the sun, and it does not rise, and seals up the stars. And this happened at the cross; and seals up the stars; it is reported that in the three hours in which the sun failed, stars appeared in heaven as at night. The one who makes the Pleiad, and Hesperus, and Arcturus, and the chambers of the south. These are teachings beyond me. For though there are many stars of the Pleiades, planets and fixed stars being enumerated by those who do not know as they think (there is also Hesperus, there is also Phaethon, and Phainon, and Stilbon and Phosphorus) why then did Job speaking in the Spirit from so many stars in the fixed sphere name only the Pleiad? and from so many so-called planets he mentioned only Hesperus? and another one, Arcturus, the one being in the bear, the one called by some the bear-keeper?

choices.why: The glossary requires 'making old' for παλαιῶν and 'mountains' for ὄρη; the participle keeps the continuous force of the Greek present.

choices.term: τὴν κατὰ τὸ γράμμα Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἢ τοῦ γράμματος
choices.english: the Jerusalem according to the letter or of the letter
choices.why: The Greek has two parallel genitive constructions: 'according to the letter' and 'of the letter'; the English keeps both distinct rather than collapsing the second into 'the letter itself.'
rejected: the Jerusalem according to the letter, or the letter itself
the letter-based Jerusalem or the letter

choices.term: ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ ἐν γράμματι ἐντετυπωμένη ἦν, φησίν
choices.english: The ministry of death was engraved in letters, it says
choices.why: The φησίν marks a Scripture quotation (2 Corinthians 3:7); placing 'it says' after the quoted clause keeps the quotation boundary clear.
rejected: The ministry of death, it says, was engraved in letters
it says the ministry of death was engraved in letters

choices.why: The glossary requires 'pillars' for στύλοι, interpreted as the apostles.
The verb means to seal or close up; 'seals up' preserves the sense of closing off the stars from view, matching the darkness at the crucifixion.
The phrase marks Job's prophetic speech; 'in the Spirit' keeps the instrumental dative force.

pass_b_english: So as long as the new covenant had not come, the prophets were not old, for nothing had been said outside of a covenant before this. But Christ is the one making old the mountains—Moses and the prophets. “And they do not know it” (Job 9:5). Who does not know it? Those to whom he said, “If you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me” (John 5:46). If the Jews had known that the mountains were being made old, they would have abandoned them—that is, the oldness of the letter—and would have passed over and come to the new covenant, and they would have worshiped God in newness of Spirit and not in oldness of letter (Romans 7:6). So he adds: the Jews do not know either the one who made them old or the things that have been made old. Therefore, he says, he is the one overturning them in wrath—that is, the Jerusalem according to the letter [or: of the letter]. Where is the perceptible altar? My Jesus has done something marvelous When he came, his own prophets he has both made old and renewed. He made them old—how? “The ministry of death was engraved in letters,” it says (2 Corinthians 3:7). He renewed them—how? “The law is holy, and its commandment is holy and just and good” (Romans 7:12). But those who did not learn the spiritual name did not know these things.

“He who shakes what is under heaven from its foundations” (Job 9:6). Christ is the one who shook what is under heaven. Many earthquakes happen in part: an earthquake happens here, but those in the neighboring city do not know it. But with Christ it did not happen partially. Therefore he is the one shaking what is under heaven from its foundations. And its pillars are shaken—clearly the apostles were shaken at the time of the passion. “All of you,” he says, “will be scandalized because of me this night” (Matthew 26:31).

“He who speaks to the sun, and it does not rise, and seals up the stars” (Job 9:7). This also happened at the cross. “And seals up the stars”: it is reported that during the three hours when the sun failed, stars appeared in the sky as at night.

“He who makes the Pleiad, and Hesperus, and Arcturus, and the chambers of the south” (Job 9:9). These matters are beyond me. For since there are many stars—Pleiads, planets and fixed stars—listed by those who do not know, as they suppose (there is Hesperus, and Phaethon, and Phainon, and Stilbon, and Phosphorus), why then did Job, speaking in the Spirit, name only the Pleiad out of so many stars in the fixed sphere? And out of so many planets spoken of, why did he mention only Hesperus? And one other, Arcturus, the one in the bear, called by some the bear-keeper?

problems.quote: Has my Jesus done something astonishing?
problems.why: παράδοξον is neuter singular, object not adverb: 'Has my Jesus done a paradox/marvelous thing?'
problems.fix: Has my Jesus done a paradox? or Has my Jesus done something strange?

problems.quote: the Jerusalem according to the letter or of the letter
problems.source_quote: τὴν κατὰ τὸ γράμμα Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἢ τοῦ γράμματος
problems.why: ἢ τοῦ γράμματος is alternative reading, not 'or of the letter'; should indicate textual variant
problems.fix: the Jerusalem according to the letter [or: of the letter]

problems.quote: he both made his prophets old and renewed them
problems.source_quote: τοὺς αὐτοῦ προφήτας καὶ πεπαλαίωκεν καὶ ἀνεκαίνισε
problems.why: τοὺς αὐτοῦ προφήτας is object of both verbs, but καὶ before πεπαλαίωκεν is emphatic, not 'both...and' exactly
problems.fix: his prophets he has made old and renewed

problems.quote: and would have been reconciled and come to the new covenant
problems.source_quote: καταλιπόντες ἂν αὐτὰ… διήλλανται καὶ ἐληλύθησαν ἐπὶ τὴν καινὴν διαθήκην
problems.why: διήλλανται means 'changed their minds' or 'passed over', not 'reconciled'; the Jews would have left the old and passed to the new.
problems.fix: and would have passed over and come to the new covenant
problems.ruling: διήλλανται from διαλλάσσομαι means 'changed'/'exchanged', not 'reconciled'; 'passed over' fits context of leaving old for new.

problems.quote: for nowhere before this is anything said about a covenant
problems.source_quote: οὐδαμοῦ γὰρ παρὰ διαθήκην, εἴρηται πρὸ τούτου
problems.why: παρὰ διαθήκην means 'contrary to covenant' or 'besides covenant', not 'about a covenant'
problems.fix: for nothing contrary to a covenant had been said before this
problems.ruling: παρὰ διαθήκην means 'contrary to/besides covenant'; 'about a covenant' misreads παρὰ as περί, changing the meaning.
